_what: Role recipes: the SQL that makes a login of a kind in the person's own database, gives it its rights, and takes it away. Each statement is a format() string of the server's own (%1$I the role, %2$L its password, %3$L the time it stops working, %4$I the database the connection names, %5$I the database the held role connection names; a recipe that adds rows also has %6$I its table, %7$s its columns, %8$L its fixed values and %9$I its trigger's name; a recipe that takes a held value (`takes_held_value`) has it as %10$L, the value held under value_credential_name, handed on descriptor 6), filled by the server so no value is ever spliced into SQL text here. The owner login runs them (it needs CREATEROLE: tools/start-a-computer set-up-postgres-role.sh PG_MAKES_ROLES=yes), in one transaction, so a recipe makes all of a role or none of it, unless it says in_one_transaction false (Postgres makes and drops a database only outside a transaction block; its statements then run one by one on one connection). Standing: valid until infinity, the password the person holds under a name. Minted: a made-up password and a VALID UNTIL time; the answer hands the login once. A recipe's limits are the per-login limits a create may set: each is one statement filled with %6$s, the value the caller gives (a whole number above zero, checked before it reaches the server), and runs after the create statements only when that value is given, so no limit is a number chosen here: the caller passes what the computer's measured capacity allows.

read-only._what: A login that may connect to the owner's database and read every table of its public schema, the ones there now and the ones the owner makes later, and may do nothing else: a share that may only read.
create: CREATE ROLE %1$I LOGIN PASSWORD %2$L VALID UNTIL %3$L
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO %1$I
drop: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE SELECT ON TABLES FROM %1$I
REVOKE SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I
DROP ROLE %1$I

own-database._what: A login and a database it owns, made by the login of whoever runs the computer (CREATEROLE and CREATEDB: set-up-postgres-role.sh PG_MAKES_ROLES=yes PG_MAKES_DATABASES=yes): each pursuit's own database, closed to every other login, the operator's too, so the computer's row names no pursuit. The role, its password and its database are the held role connection's (role_credential_name), which only its owner holds. Postgres lets a login make a database another role owns, or act for that owner, only while it may SET ROLE to it, so the operator takes that right for these statements and gives it back; it stays the role's admin, which lets it reset a lost password.
create: CREATE ROLE %1$I LOGIN PASSWORD %2$L
GRANT %1$I TO CURRENT_USER WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE
CREATE DATABASE %5$I OWNER %1$I
SET ROLE %1$I
REVOKE ALL ON DATABASE %5$I FROM PUBLIC
RESET ROLE
REVOKE SET OPTION FOR %1$I FROM CURRENT_USER
drop: GRANT %1$I TO CURRENT_USER WITH SET TRUE, INHERIT FALSE
SET ROLE %1$I
DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS %5$I
RESET ROLE
DROP ROLE %1$I

may-change-rows._what: A login that may connect to the owner's database and read, add, change and remove rows of every table of its public schema, the ones there now and the ones the owner makes later, and use their counters, and may do nothing else: a member of a pursuit who works in its rows but never changes its tables, makes logins or reaches another database. Removing them is the drop.
create: CREATE ROLE %1$I LOGIN PASSWORD %2$L VALID UNTIL %3$L
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO %1$I
drop: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES FROM %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I
DROP ROLE %1$I

a-login._what: Only a login: the role and its password, with no right in any database, made by a login that may make roles (CREATEROLE) where the database's own owner may not. Its rights come from a grants-only recipe the database's owner runs in that database (may-change-rows-for-a-login). The drop takes the login away once its rights are taken back.
create: CREATE ROLE %1$I LOGIN PASSWORD %2$L VALID UNTIL %3$L
drop: DROP ROLE %1$I

may-change-rows-for-a-login._what: The rights of may-change-rows given to a login another login made (a-login), run by the database's owner in that database: read, add, change and remove rows of every table of its public schema, now and later, and use their counters; never change a table, make a login or reach another database. It makes and drops no login, so its owner needs no right to make roles. The drop takes the rights back and leaves the login.
create: GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES TO %1$I
drop: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE USAGE, SELECT ON SEQUENCES FROM %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON TABLES FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE, SELECT ON ALL SEQUENCES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I

may-only-add-rows-for-a-login._what: The rights of a login that may only add rows of one table, given to a login another login made (a-login), run by the database's owner in that database: it may connect and add rows, naming only recipe.columns, and read, change or remove nothing, in that table or any other. The row itself is held to a rule: each recipe.fixed column is set by the server to its value on every row this login adds, whatever the login sends, and a column that is neither listed nor fixed cannot be named at all (the column grant refuses it). Chosen over row-level security because turning row security on for a table blanks it for every other login without a policy of its own, and over an insert function because the login should add rows with the same INSERT every other writer uses. The login has no SELECT, so an INSERT answers no rows back (RETURNING is refused) and ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE is refused; a row whose key already exists is refused with the server's own duplicate-key text (or adds nothing under ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), which says only that the key is taken. %6$I is recipe.table, %7$s recipe.columns each quoted and joined, %8$L recipe.fixed as JSON text, %9$I the trigger's name (rule_ and the role). The trigger acts only for this role, so the owner's and every other login's rows are untouched; its function is shared by every login of this kind. It makes and drops no login. The drop takes the trigger and every right back and leaves the login.
create: GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION public.hold_added_rows_to_their_rule() RETURNS trigger LANGUAGE plpgsql AS $body$ BEGIN IF current_user = TG_ARGV[0] THEN NEW := jsonb_populate_record(NEW, TG_ARGV[1]::jsonb); END IF; RETURN NEW; END $body$
GRANT INSERT (%7$s) ON TABLE %6$I TO %1$I
CREATE TRIGGER %9$I BEFORE INSERT ON %6$I FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION public.hold_added_rows_to_their_rule(%1$L, %8$L)
drop: DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS %9$I ON %6$I
REVOKE ALL ON TABLE %6$I FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I

post-writer-for-a-login._what: The rights of a post writer given to a login another login made (a-login), run by the pursuit's owner in its own database: it may connect, read the article site destinations (article_site_destinations) and read, add and change posts (post) under the post table's row rules (consent_fence). It may not change a destination's SQL, a table, or any other table, and it may not make logins. The drop takes the rights back.
create: GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT ON TABLE public.article_site_destinations TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON TABLE public.post TO %1$I
drop: REVOKE SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE ON TABLE public.post FROM %1$I
REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE public.article_site_destinations FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I

may-read-under-row-rules._what: The rights of a login another login made (a-login) that reads a pursuit's rows only under the row rules, for runs whose use the engine binds: it may connect and read every table of the public schema, the ones there now and the ones the owner makes later, and may change nothing, make nothing (temporary tables included: TEMPORARY on the database is taken from it and from PUBLIC, so no table of its own can stand in for one a rule reads) and reach no other database; a login that bypasses row rules, is a superuser, or may act as the owner is refused. Run by the database's owner in that database. It also keeps the use binding the row rules read (schema use_binding): the held value on descriptor 6 (value_credential_name, the computer's <database>-use-key) is the key the engine signs each run's use ticket with; use_binding.claim_use(ticket) checks the ticket's HMAC-SHA256 and its end and binds its purpose and surface to the calling transaction once (the ticket's nonce cannot be claimed twice); use_binding.run_purpose() and run_surface() answer the claimed use, and a transaction with no claim the pursuit's own use_settings row purpose_when_unstated (no row: no purpose, so nothing is allowed). The login cannot read or change the keys or the claims (they live in a schema it may only call into), and no setting a session may SET is read. The drop takes the login's rights back; the binding and its keys stay for the next login.
create: DO $check$ BEGIN IF (SELECT rolsuper OR rolbypassrls FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = %1$L) OR pg_catalog.pg_has_role(%1$L, current_user, 'MEMBER') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'The login %% may get round the row rules (a superuser, one that bypasses row rules, or a member of the owner); give a login a-login made.', %1$L; END IF; END $check$
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS use_binding
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA use_binding TO PUBLIC
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto WITH SCHEMA use_binding
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS use_binding.ticket_keys (key text PRIMARY KEY, added_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now())

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS use_binding.claims (nonce text PRIMARY KEY, xact xid8 NOT NULL UNIQUE, purpose text, surface text, claimed_by name NOT NULL, claimed_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), until timestamptz NOT NULL)
REVOKE ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA use_binding FROM PUBLIC
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS public.use_settings (name text PRIMARY KEY, value text NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO use_binding.ticket_keys (key) VALUES (%10$L) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION use_binding.claim_use(ticket text) RETURNS TABLE (purpose text, surface text) LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, use_binding, public, pg_temp AS $body$ DECLARE parts text[] := string_to_array(ticket, '.'); payload jsonb; ends timestamptz; BEGIN IF array_length(parts, 1) IS DISTINCT FROM 2 OR parts[1] !~ '^([0-9a-f]{2})+$' OR parts[2] !~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'That is not a use ticket.' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END IF; IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM use_binding.ticket_keys k WHERE encode(hmac(convert_to(parts[1], 'UTF8'), convert_to(k.key, 'UTF8'), 'sha256'), 'hex') = parts[2]) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'The use ticket was not signed with a key this database keeps.' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END IF; payload := convert_from(decode(parts[1], 'hex'), 'UTF8')::jsonb; ends := to_timestamp((payload->>'until')::numeric / 1000); IF ends <= clock_timestamp() THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'The use ticket has ended.' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END IF; DELETE FROM use_binding.claims c WHERE c.until < clock_timestamp(); BEGIN INSERT INTO use_binding.claims (nonce, xact, purpose, surface, claimed_by, until) VALUES (payload->>'nonce', pg_current_xact_id(), payload->>'purpose', payload->>'surface', session_user, ends); EXCEPTION WHEN unique_violation THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'The use ticket was claimed already, or this transaction holds a use.' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END; RETURN QUERY SELECT payload->>'purpose', payload->>'surface'; END $body$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION use_binding.run_purpose() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, use_binding, pg_temp AS $body$ SELECT CASE WHEN c.nonce IS NOT NULL AND c.purpose IS NOT NULL THEN c.purpose ELSE (SELECT s.value FROM public.use_settings s WHERE s.name = 'purpose_when_unstated') END FROM (SELECT pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned() AS xact) t LEFT JOIN use_binding.claims c ON c.xact = t.xact $body$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION use_binding.run_surface() RETURNS text LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, use_binding, pg_temp AS $body$ SELECT coalesce(c.surface, '') FROM (SELECT pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned() AS xact) t LEFT JOIN use_binding.claims c ON c.xact = t.xact $body$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION use_binding.fenced(t regclass) RETURNS TABLE (fenced boolean, claimed_purpose text, allowed boolean) LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, use_binding, pg_temp AS $body$ SELECT c.relrowsecurity AND c.relforcerowsecurity, (SELECT cl.purpose FROM use_binding.claims cl WHERE cl.xact = pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned()), has_table_privilege(session_user, c.oid, 'SELECT') FROM pg_class c WHERE c.oid = t $body$
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION use_binding.fenced(regclass) TO %1$I
REVOKE TEMPORARY ON DATABASE %4$I FROM PUBLIC, %1$I
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
drop: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE SELECT ON TABLES FROM %1$I
REVOKE SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA public FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I
may-read-under-row-rules._public_grants_what: The whole public schema, read by the login: USAGE, SELECT on every table there now and later. Given only when no recipe.tables are named; with recipe.tables the login reads exactly those tables and their schemas' USAGE (a public table with no row rule, such as a consent table, is then not readable).

create: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO %1$I
ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public GRANT SELECT ON TABLES TO %1$I

may-read-under-row-rules._per_table_what: Named tables (recipe.tables, each schema.table) the login may read in a schema other than public. Only the named table is granted: a schema's other tables may hold rows no row rule guards (a subject's name, a consent record), so no whole-schema SELECT and no default privilege is given here. An entry may be { table: schema.table, columns: [...] } instead: then only those columns are readable (a table holding a note or a link no page shows). %11$I is the schema, %12$I the table, %13$s the server-quoted columns in brackets, or nothing for the whole table.

create: GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA %11$I TO %1$I
GRANT SELECT %13$s ON TABLE %11$I.%12$I TO %1$I
drop: REVOKE SELECT ON TABLE %11$I.%12$I FROM %1$I
REVOKE USAGE ON SCHEMA %11$I FROM %1$I

may-write-named-columns-under-a-use._what: The rights of a login another login made (a-login) that writes only the named columns of the named tables of a pursuit's database, for runs whose use the engine binds (the tool row's credential item says under_use with held_suffix -writer-connection): it may connect, call the use binding's claim, and per recipe.writes entry read, add or change exactly the columns named, remove rows only where the entry says delete, and run only the functions named (an owner-made SECURITY DEFINER function stands in for a read the login must not hold, such as a token it matches on). It may make nothing (temporary tables included: TEMPORARY on the database is taken from it and from PUBLIC), reach no other database and hold no default privilege; a login that bypasses row rules, is a superuser, or may act as the owner is refused. Run by the database's owner in that database, after may-read-under-row-rules has made the use binding (it is refused without one: the key and the claims are that recipe's). The drop takes every right on each named table and function back (a table's REVOKE ALL takes its column rights too) and leaves the login.
create: DO $check$ BEGIN IF (SELECT rolsuper OR rolbypassrls FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = %1$L) OR pg_catalog.pg_has_role(%1$L, current_user, 'MEMBER') THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'The login %% may get round the row rules (a superuser, one that bypasses row rules, or a member of the owner); give a login a-login made.', %1$L; END IF; END $check$

DO $check$ BEGIN IF pg_catalog.to_regprocedure('use_binding.claim_use(text)') IS NULL THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'This database has no use binding: run may-read-under-row-rules first, so a writer''s runs claim a use the database keeps a key for.'; END IF; END $check$
REVOKE TEMPORARY ON DATABASE %4$I FROM PUBLIC, %1$I
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I TO %1$I
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION use_binding.claim_use(text) TO %1$I
drop: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION use_binding.claim_use(text) FROM %1$I
REVOKE CONNECT ON DATABASE %4$I FROM %1$I
may-write-named-columns-under-a-use._per_write_what: Each recipe.writes entry is { table: schema.table, select?, insert?, update?: [column, ...], delete?: true } or { function: 'schema.name(argument types)' }. Each right the entry names is one statement below, %11$I the schema, %12$I the table and %13$s the server-quoted columns (or the function the server resolves by to_regprocedure); a right the entry does not name is never granted. The drop runs the drop statements once per entry. A table entry may also name `rows: { key: column }`: the login then reads, adds and changes only the rows whose key column holds the digest of a key its run presented in the same transaction, after it claimed its use (use_binding.present_key(key): the words page's ask token, say), so a run that holds one row's key reaches that row and no other. The key column is made (text, empty in every row there now, so the login reaches none of them). A table whose row rules were off has them switched on together with rows_as_they_were, which lets every other login under row rules (a reader, another writer) read and write as it did before (the owner and the logins that are its members are not under row rules at all); a table that already had row rules keeps its own, and its other logins' rules are not loosened. The login's own rule (%9$I) is restrictive, so it holds on top of whatever lets the login reach a row. `keeps_out: { column: [key, ...] }` names keys of a jsonb column the login may never write a value into (an approval it must not give itself). %13$s is the server-quoted key column, or the rule's USING and WITH CHECK the server writes from the entry. The drop takes the login's rule away and leaves the key column, the row rules and rows_as_they_were, which other logins' rules and the rows themselves may rest on.

row_binding: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS use_binding.presented_keys (xact xid8 NOT NULL, key_digest text NOT NULL, until timestamptz NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (xact, key_digest))
REVOKE ALL ON TABLE use_binding.presented_keys FROM PUBLIC

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION use_binding.present_key(key text) RETURNS void LANGUAGE plpgsql VOLATILE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, use_binding, pg_temp AS $body$ BEGIN IF key IS NULL OR length(key) < 16 THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'A row key is at least 16 characters.' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END IF; IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM use_binding.claims c WHERE c.xact = pg_current_xact_id()) THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'A row key is presented only in a transaction that claimed its use.' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'; END IF; DELETE FROM use_binding.presented_keys p WHERE p.until < clock_timestamp(); INSERT INTO use_binding.presented_keys (xact, key_digest, until) VALUES (pg_current_xact_id(), encode(sha256(convert_to(key, 'UTF8')), 'hex'), clock_timestamp() + interval '1 hour') ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; END $body$

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION use_binding.presented_keys() RETURNS text[] LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = pg_catalog, use_binding, pg_temp AS $body$ SELECT coalesce(array_agg(p.key_digest), '{}') FROM use_binding.presented_keys p WHERE p.xact = pg_current_xact_id_if_assigned() $body$
REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION use_binding.present_key(text), use_binding.presented_keys() FROM PUBLIC
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION use_binding.present_key(text), use_binding.presented_keys() TO %1$I
create.row_key: ALTER TABLE %11$I.%12$I ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS %13$s text
row_rules: DO $rule$ BEGIN IF NOT (SELECT c.relrowsecurity FROM pg_catalog.pg_class c WHERE c.oid = pg_catalog.format('%%I.%%I', %11$L, %12$L)::regclass) THEN CREATE POLICY rows_as_they_were ON %11$I.%12$I AS PERMISSIVE FOR ALL TO PUBLIC USING (true) WITH CHECK (true); ALTER TABLE %11$I.%12$I ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY; END IF; END $rule$
CREATE POLICY %9$I ON %11$I.%12$I AS RESTRICTIVE FOR ALL TO %1$I %13$s

row_binding: REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTION use_binding.present_key(text), use_binding.presented_keys() FROM %1$I
